description.narrative: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is the expansion of access to finance for MSMEs including WSMEs in Senegal which is particularly challenging for MSMEs. Beyond the project-level outcomes, IFC anticipates that this Project will contribute to market creation as through financial integration, by supporting the first private sector sustainable bond in the WAEMU capital market at a 5-year tenor and could potentially serve as a demonstration of the use of local capital markets to raise long-term local currency funding for impact intensive assets.

The proposed project consists of an anchor investment of up to XOF5 billion (US$8.4 million equivalent) in Baobab Senegal (BBSN)s Sustainable Bond Issuance (XOF20 billion or about US$33.7 million), the first from the private sector in the WAEMU. This investment will take the form of an unfunded risk participation for the African Local Currency Bond Fund Limited SICAV-RAIF (ALCBF or the Fund), a dedicated pan-African structured debt fund and an IFC client that will invest on IFC's behalf. At least 40 percent of the Bond proceeds will support women-owned/led MSMEs (WMSMEs) (the Project). Despite the unfunded participation through ALCBF, IFC will have direct recourse to BBSN in the event of a material policy breach.
